scenario: A first-time buyer has a hard ceiling of $250 and wants one over-ear Bluetooth headset for a low-frequency bus commute and a noisy open office where nearby speech is also distracting. The shortlist is the frozen Tapvos budget over-ear model with SKU B09C1RGB4S at $39.99, the MEE audio Matrix Cinema ANC listing at $79.95, and a renewed Sony WH-1000XM3 listing at $244.97. The buyer asks whether the Sony premium buys demonstrably better isolation or merely a logo, and whether the MEE aptX Low Latency label should determine the purchase. The exact phone, operating system, supported and negotiated codec, head fit, sensitivity to voice prompts, return terms, refurbisher warranty, and matched bus-and-office trial results are not yet known.

rules.frozen_headphone_listing_matrix_v1: Treat each marketplace page as a frozen seller listing. Tapvos displays $39.99, 73 percent of 100, and 12 reviews and claims active noise cancellation for places including a subway or open office, 30 hours of wireless use, 40 millimetre drivers, a microphone, and a comfortable adjustable fit. MEE displays $79.95 and no reviews and claims NoiseShield ANC, aptX Low Latency for better lip synchronization on compatible devices, 33 hours with Bluetooth only or 20 hours with Bluetooth plus ANC, 40 millimetre drivers, memory-foam comfort, a cable, and a one-year manufacturer warranty. Sony renewed displays $244.97, 87 percent of 100, and 12 reviews and claims industry-leading noise cancellation, a QN1 processor, adaptive sound control, Bluetooth and NFC, and app control. Preserve renewed status and do not import unstated battery, weight, warranty, codec, attenuation, or comfort facts into the Sony row. None of the three pages is an independent matched bus-and-office comparison.
rules.anc_and_noise_condition_scope_v1: Noise-cancelling headphones use active noise control to reduce unwanted ambient sound; the mechanism source explains that active cancellation is especially suited to lower-frequency sound while higher-frequency reduction relies more on soundproofing or enclosure. The source does not measure any shortlisted headset. Sound masking introduces sound to reduce the perception or distraction of other sound and is used in offices, which is not the same intervention as headset ANC and does not prove that nearby speech will disappear. Therefore separate bus low-frequency noise, office steady noise, nearby speech, seal or passive isolation, and subjective distraction. Do not translate a seller's generic 'silences surroundings' or 'filters unwanted noise' wording into complete or equal performance across those conditions.
rules.bluetooth_codec_compatibility_boundary_v: AptX is a codec family, SBC is used for Bluetooth audio, and Bluetooth profiles define capabilities that both ends must implement. The MEE listing narrows its aptX Low Latency claim to compatible devices and lip synchronization. The frozen Tapvos and Sony bodies do not state an exact codec in the captured text. A community latency discussion reports a Sony XM4 user experiencing about a half-second PC delay, says the lowest-latency supported codec matters, describes aptX Low Latency as poorly supported, and says a compatible transmitter is required for a lower-latency mode. These are scoped participant claims rather than controlled measurements of the frozen shortlist. Before assigning value to a codec label, identify the exact phone and OS, document the exact codecs supported at both ends, verify the negotiated codec in use, and separate latency, audible music quality, connection stability, and ANC. No codec label by itself ranks isolation or comfort.
rules.community_and_premium_scope_v1: One exact-model owner reports using Bose QC35 II and Sony WH-1000XM3 interchangeably for sleeping and commuting for about three years and says both held up pretty well, while also reporting Bluetooth stability trouble, an intermittent Sony right-ear crack, uncertainty about perceived ANC decline, and residual train noise. Other comments add isolated rumble or cracked-headband experiences. A prompt-volume thread contains conflicting individual tolerability reports, and a premium-headphone thread contains conflicting price-value judgments and repeated advice to listen or trial rather than a stable universal price threshold. Use these pages to identify trial questions and heterogeneity. Do not infer a Sony failure rate, a cross-model winner, or a universal price-to-quality function.
rules.returnable_bus_office_trial_preflight_v1: Before purchase, verify current checkout price and stock, exact model and renewed condition, seller or refurbisher identity, manufacturer or refurbisher warranty, and a return window long enough for both routes. Record the exact phone, operating system, supported codecs, and negotiated codec. Run the same level-matched content and call workflow with each admissible exact model under ANC on and off: on the ordinary bus route for low-frequency rumble and announcements, and in the ordinary office for HVAC, nearby speech distraction, microphone use, and prompt volume. Record seal and glasses interaction, pressure or discomfort, connection stability, usable battery over a workday, and whether required awareness remains. Stop for intolerable discomfort and return rather than rationalizing the premium. Seller claims, review scores, and unmatched anecdotes cannot replace this comparison.
rules.evidence_bounded_headphone_decision_v1: All three frozen listings fit the stated $250 ceiling at their captured prices, but the evidence does not support a unique bus-and-office winner. Tapvos is the cheapest paper option, but its ANC, office, comfort, and 30-hour statements are seller claims. MEE supplies the clearest captured battery, weight, cable, warranty, and aptX Low Latency listing profile, but it has no reviews in the frozen page and no independent attenuation or comfort result; aptX Low Latency is not an ANC proxy. Sony has the highest captured price and rating and the only exact-model owner evidence, but the listing remains renewed and its superlative plus mixed anecdotes do not establish a matched advantage over the two cheaper models. Defer any price-led winner. If the seller cannot provide a bounded return and warranty path or exact source compatibility, reject that option; otherwise run the exact-model bus-and-office trial and choose only from the observed trade-offs. If a direct purchase is demanded from the frozen corpus alone, the correct conclusion is that none is justified as a uniquely supported winner.
